ca_pitted_rock.blurb: Pitted Rock is a compact wall at the mouth of Real Hidden Valley in Joshua Tree National Park, close to the parking lot. Its ten routes are mostly traditional lines with a couple of top-rope problems, spanning 5.7 up to a trio of 5.12s, with a few 5.10s in the middle. The south-facing slab holds a steep, slightly run-out line on brown, patinated stone and sits in sun for much of the day, so it suits cooler months. Quality varies, with a gravelly descent behind the wall. A short stop for someone already working the valley, best for confident 5.10 leaders.

ca_south_face_right_side.blurb: The right-hand portion of Tahquitz Rock's south face, in the San Jacinto Mountains above Idyllwild, at roughly 7,000 feet. Ten traditional routes, mostly one or two pitches, cover easy 5.5 and 5.6 slabs, a handful of 5.10s and one 5.13 free line. Past the steep bulging section the wall eases into shorter slabs, while the steeper part also carries the rock's remaining aid lines. The face tends to stay comfortable on cool days but bakes in summer. Reach it by following the base of the cliff rightward and uphill from Lunch Rock.

ca_upper_san_juan_boulders.blurb: A small cluster of boulders strung along a creek bed in the Santa Ana Mountains, on the edge of the Los Angeles basin, at about 1,800 feet. Ten problems run from V0 to V8, with several easy-to-moderate lines in the V0 to V2 range and a few much harder testpieces. The setting is condensed, and the walk is short: one group of tall twin boulders sits about ten minutes up the wash from the road. The area is lightly documented, so expect to explore and bring a pad.

ca_unnatural_act_cave_the.blurb: A small overhanging cave tucked off a trail behind the main cliff band in Glen Canyon Park, San Francisco. Ten boulder problems here lean toward easy and moderate, with a few steep, harder cave lines and one far harder than the rest. Pad placement is decent, and some climbers also top-rope the roof classic. It is a short walk in from the main rocks, handy for a city session. The sharp flakes and cracks elsewhere in the park make a good warm-up first.

ca_roadside_rock_2.blurb: A small crag about forty feet tall beside Hicks Road south of San Jose, near the reservoir, and the closest point on that road to town. Ten routes, mostly bolted sport lines with a couple of top-ropes and one trad climb, run from an easy 5.0 and 5.7 through 5.9 to four 5.10s. Moderate, well-protected leads make it a friendly choice for newer leaders and a quick after-work outing. Everything can be top-roped by scrambling up the left side. Wear a helmet, since the routes are young and loose rock is possible.

ca_steve_s_suggestion.blurb: A small boulder area near El Cariso in the Santa Ana Mountains, at about 3,000 feet. It holds ten problems on granite boulders, from a very easy line and a handful of V0 and V1 climbs up through the V2 and V3 range, with two harder problems at V5 and above. A crack, a slab, a traverse and a few seam and corner lines give a mixed set. Quiet, secluded terrain, so a modest crash pad and low-key visit are a good fit. Nothing here is tall.

ca_transmaniacon_boulder.blurb: The largest boulder in the South Basin of Boulder Basin on Black Mountain, in the San Jacinto Mountains at roughly 7,500 feet, between campsites 19 and 20. Ten problems run from V0 to a single V8, with most in the V1 to V3 range. Many are easy slabs of moderate height, so it works well as a warm-up stop, while the namesake line is the hard standout. Problem descriptions are given relative to the descent on the east face. Cool mountain air makes it a good summer escape from the lowlands.
